summary: How often numbers are checked, such as every month, every season or every year.
example: Monthly Cycle: the numbers on it are checked once a month.
definition: How often something is reported, and when each round is due: either equal periods (the length of one period in months and the month the cycle's year starts) or named periods listed by the month each ends (terms each year, survey waves once), and how many days after a period closes the report is due. A KPI names one, and the periods its readings are recorded for are derived from it, never stored again; a period is named by the month it ends. One cycle is shared by every measure read on that rhythm. A reporting cycle is not a data source's refresh (how often the numbers in the source change), not a horizon (the span an aim covers), and not a single report or its audience.

/spec/periodMonths.guide: How many months one period covers: 1, 3, 6 or 12. Choose the rhythm the sources can actually supply.

poor.text: 1, for measures read from forms transcribed once a season
poor.why: Two months in three would have nothing to read; the period is as short as the source allows, no shorter.

/spec/startMonth.guide: The month of the year the first period opens, from 1 to 12. Periods are laid out from it, so it decides which month each period ends in.
good: 9, for a cooperative whose season year opens in September

poor.text: 1, for a seasonal cycle when the season year opens in September
poor.why: Periods would end in March, June, September and December, cutting across the seasons the readings describe.

/spec/periods.guide: Named periods, for a rhythm equal months cannot hold: terms of four, four and three months, or survey waves that follow a protocol rather than a calendar. Give each its name and the month it ends: a month of the year for one that repeats, listed in the order the year runs; a year and month for one that happens once. A missed term or wave still shows as a period with no reading. Use equal periods instead whenever they fit.
good: Term I ends in month 12, Term II in 4, Term III in 7

poor.text: Quarterly, for readings taken at the end of each term
poor.why: Quarters end in March, June, September and December, which are not when terms end. Name the terms instead.
With no periods, a missed reading cannot show. Name the waves by the month each ends.

/spec/periods/-/name.guide: What the period is called, as people say it. Each name is used once.

/spec/periods/-/endMonth.guide: For a period that repeats each year: the month it ends, 1 to 12. The year starts the month after the last period ends.

/spec/periods/-/end.guide: For a period that happens once: the year and month it ends.

/spec/dueOffsetDays.guide: How many days after a period closes the report is due, allowing for the time the figures take to arrive.
good: 14, for a seasonal cycle whose forms are transcribed in the two weeks after the season

poor.text: 0, when the figures take weeks to transcribe
poor.why: Every round would be late on the day it closes.

/metadata/name.guide: The name, as people say it and as lists show it.

KPI:/spec/cycle.ask: Which KPIs are read on this cycle?
KPI:/spec/cycle.ifNone: Nothing has to be defined first: a cycle stands on its own, and a KPI names it when its means of verification are set.
